Policy Name: Cigna Lumbar Fusion (CMM-609: Lumbar Fusion with Decompression)
Referred Sections: CMM-609.4: Lumbar Fusion (Arthrodesis) with Decompression (Indirect or Direct)
Second or Greater Recurrent Disc Herniation

Required findings: Individual is a candidate for lumbar decompression or lumbar corpectomy per CMM-608: Lumbar Decompression.

Imaging findings include degenerative spondylolisthesis without spondylolysis with EITHER dynamic segmental instability on flexion-extension plain x-rays OR comparison of a supine and upright image (difference in translational alignment >3mm) OR Meyerding Grade II or higher spondylolisthesis.

OR imaging findings include spondylolisthesis with spondylolysis (e.g., Isthmic Spondylolisthesis) with ANY of: Meyerding Grade I or II spondylolisthesis with plain x-rays supporting progression; Meyerding Grade III or higher spondylolisthesis with ≥50% anterior slippage OR plain x-rays supporting progression; progressive spinal pain without confirmatory imaging showing progression; multi-level spondylolysis on plain x-rays; post-operative instability from facet joint excision exceeding 50% bilaterally or 75% of a single facet; pars fracture; or previous spinal decompression resulting in iatrogenic spondylolisthesis.

Documentation of nicotine-free status: individual is a never-smoker OR has refrained from smoking, smokeless tobacco, and nicotine replacement therapy for at least six (6) weeks prior to surgery, validated by objective cotinine testing (serum, urinary, or saliva) verified as within normal range.

Required findings: Individual is a candidate for lumbar decompression or lumbar corpectomy per CMM-608: Lumbar Decompression.

Anticipated iatrogenic instability created by ANY of: disruption of posterior elements due to facet joint excision exceeding 50% bilaterally or 75% of a single facet; removal of the pars interarticularis requiring fusion; decompression for Meyerding Grade I or higher spondylolisthesis with foraminal stenosis; or complete or partial corpectomy (removal of at least one-third of the vertebral body, not for osteophyte resection alone).

Documentation of nicotine-free status: individual is a never-smoker OR has refrained from smoking, smokeless tobacco, and nicotine replacement therapy for at least six (6) weeks prior to surgery, validated by objective cotinine testing (serum, urinary, or saliva) verified as within normal range.

Required findings: Individual is a candidate for lumbar decompression or lumbar corpectomy per CMM-608: Lumbar Decompression.

Imaging findings include EITHER coronal plane deformity (Cobb angle >30°, asymmetric disk collapse causing symptomatic foraminal narrowing, or global coronal imbalance causing head and trunk shift off midline) OR sagittal imbalance (sagittal vertebral axis measurement >8cm or pelvic incidence-lumbar lordosis >15°).

Documentation of nicotine-free status: individual is a never-smoker OR has refrained from smoking, smokeless tobacco, and nicotine replacement therapy for at least six (6) weeks prior to surgery, validated by objective cotinine testing (serum, urinary, or saliva) verified as within normal range.
Medical necessity indications.Source: CMM-609.4: Lumbar Fusion (Arthrodesis) with Decompression (Indirect or Direct) > Adult Symptomatic Degenerative Spinal Deformity (TOC: S7.1.3)

Required findings: Individual is a candidate for an initial primary lumbar discectomy per CMM-606.2: Initial Primary Lumbar Microdiscectomy or CMM 606.1: General Guidelines.

Advanced imaging shows ANY of: primary extraforaminal disc herniation at L5-S1 where far lateral approach is not feasible due to iliac wings; primary foraminal disc herniation requiring facet resection for retrieval resulting in iatrogenic instability; or primary disc herniation at the level of the spinal cord (low lying conus medullaris).

Documentation of nicotine-free status: individual is a never-smoker OR has refrained from smoking, smokeless tobacco, and nicotine replacement therapy for at least six (6) weeks prior to surgery, validated by objective cotinine testing (serum, urinary, or saliva) verified as within normal range.
Medical necessity indications.Source: CMM-609.4: Lumbar Fusion (Arthrodesis) with Decompression (Indirect or Direct) > Initial Disc Herniation (TOC: S7.1.4)

Required findings: Individual is a candidate for repeat lumbar discectomy per CMM 606.3: Repeat Lumbar Microdiscectomy (Laminotomy or Laminectomy) at the Same Level.

Imaging findings include evidence of anterolisthesis at the requested level(s) resulting in EITHER dynamic segmental instability on flexion-extension plain x-rays OR comparison of a supine and upright image (difference in translational alignment >3mm) OR Meyerding Grade II or higher spondylolisthesis.

Documentation of nicotine-free status: individual is a never-smoker OR has refrained from smoking, smokeless tobacco, and nicotine replacement therapy for at least six (6) weeks prior to surgery, validated by objective cotinine testing (serum, urinary, or saliva) verified as within normal range.

Required findings: Individual is a candidate for repeat lumbar discectomy per CMM 606.3: Repeat Lumbar Microdiscectomy (Laminotomy or Laminectomy) at the Same Level.

Documentation of nicotine-free status: individual is a never-smoker OR has refrained from smoking, smokeless tobacco, and nicotine replacement therapy for at least six (6) weeks prior to surgery, validated by objective cotinine testing (serum, urinary, or saliva) verified as within normal range.
Medical necessity indications.Source: CMM-609.4: Lumbar Fusion (Arthrodesis) with Decompression (Indirect or Direct) > Second or Greater Recurrent Disc Herniation (TOC: S7.1.6)

Non-Indications: Lumbar fusion is not medically necessary if the individual has not met the specific imaging criteria for the claimed condition (e.g., Meyerding Grade I spondylolisthesis without progression or instability for Actual Instability, or Cobb angle ≤30° for coronal deformity).
Lumbar fusion is not medically necessary if the individual has not documented nicotine-free status (never-smoker or 6-week abstinence with normal cotinine test) prior to the planned surgery.

Lumbar fusion is not medically necessary for instability created or identified intra-operatively if the specific imaging criteria for 'Actual Instability' are not met, unless it falls under 'Anticipated Iatrogenic Instability' criteria.

Lumbar fusion is not medically necessary for corpectomy performed solely for the resection of osteophytes (must be removal of at least one-third of the vertebral body for Anticipated Iatrogenic Instability).
Important criteria & exceptions: Criteria exception: When instability is created and/or identified intra-operatively, the imaging criteria for 'Actual Instability' are NOT required, provided the case fits 'Anticipated Iatrogenic Instability' or other applicable sections.
Nicotine-free status must be validated by objective cotinine testing methods (serum, urinary, or saliva) verified as within the normal range for the specific testing method and lab.
For 'Actual Instability' involving spondylolisthesis with spondylolysis, progressive spinal pain without confirmatory imaging showing progression is an accepted imaging finding.
Documentation required: Objective cotinine testing results (serum, urinary, or saliva) verified as within normal range, or documentation of never-smoker status.
Dynamic segmental instability imaging: flexion-extension plain x-rays OR comparison of supine and upright images showing >3mm translational alignment difference.
Plain x-rays supporting progression of anterolisthesis (for spondylolisthesis with spondylolysis).
Advanced imaging (MRI/CT) showing primary extraforaminal, foraminal, or spinal cord level disc herniation (for Initial Disc Herniation).
Imaging evidence of anterolisthesis at the requested level(s) (for Recurrent Disc Herniation).
Imaging measurements for deformity: Cobb angle, sagittal vertebral axis, pelvic incidence-lumbar lordosis, or evidence of asymmetric disk collapse/global coronal imbalance.
Documentation of facet joint excision percentage (exceeding 50% bilaterally or 75% single facet) or pars interarticularis removal (for Anticipated Iatrogenic Instability).
Documentation of corpectomy extent (removal of at least one-third of vertebral body) if applicable.
